pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Goodnight Moon
work.note: Goodnight Moon é um livro infantil escrito por Margaret Wise Brown e publicado em 1947 nos Estados Unidos. A obra dá contexto à missão linguística — “falar do sono: fall asleep (pegar no sono) e stay up (ficar acordado)”. A referência mostra a hora de dormir: fall asleep, stay up.

facts.label: Pedir silêncio
facts.sub: Bata na porta, comece com “Sorry to bother you” e diga o problema de forma suave. Frases curtas e calmas costumam resolver.

facts.label: Bater na porta
facts.sub: Nos EUA, muita gente prefere falar diretamente com o vizinho antes de reclamar com o síndico. Bata de forma leve, sorria e comece com “Sorry to bother you”. Evite ir à porta muito tarde sem necessidade, ou com tom bravo.

facts.label: Horário de silêncio
facts.sub: Muitos prédios e cidades têm regras para barulho à noite, mas os horários mudam de lugar para lugar. Leia o contrato de aluguel ou os avisos do prédio. Se tiver dúvida, pergunte ao síndico ou ao dono do prédio.

compare.br: In Brazil, many people feel okay about parties and loud music on weekends, and neighbors often talk face to face.
compare.us: In the USA, many people ask for quiet in a very soft way, with “a little loud” and “Sorry to bother you.”
compare.tip: Say: “Sorry to bother you. Could you turn it down, please?”
compare.ask: How do you ask a neighbor for quiet? Say it in English.

pages.title: Leia: sign in a building hallway
Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In the USA, it is normal to knock and ask a neighbor to turn the volume down.
items.why: A calm, polite request is the usual first step.

items.s: You should shout through the wall at night.
items.why: Shouting makes more noise and can make the neighbor angry.

items.s: “Sorry to bother you” is a polite way to start.
items.why: It tells the person you know you are interrupting.

pages.title: A little loud · 1/3
paragraphs: Mia lives in an apartment in **Boston**. It is eleven o’clock at night. She is in bed, but she cannot sleep. Her neighbor Theo has a TV and loud music. The wall is thin, and she hears every song. She has work early in the morning.
Mia puts on her jacket and knocks on his door. She is a little nervous, but she smiles. “**Hi. Sorry to bother you**,” she says. “**No problem. What’s up?**” Theo asks.

pages.title: A little loud · 2/3
paragraphs: “**The music is a little loud.**” “**Oh, I’m so sorry!**” “**It’s late, and I have to sleep.**” Mia speaks in a soft voice. She does not shout.
“**I understand. I’ll turn it down.**” Theo goes back and turns the volume down. “**I didn’t know it was so loud**,” he says. “**It’s okay. It happens**,” Mia says. “**Thank you very much.**”

paragraphs: Back in bed, Mia thinks about a children’s book, “Goodnight Moon.” In the book, a little rabbit says goodnight to the room, the moon and the stars. Now Mia’s room is quiet. “**Sleep tight**,” she says to herself, and she closes her eyes.

pages.focus: o som do th em bother
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O th de bother é vozeado: a língua fica entre os dentes e a voz vibra. Brasileiros costumam trocar por d ou z e dizer “bóder”.
pages.how: Coloque a ponta da língua levemente entre os dentes da frente e deixe o ar sair enquanto a garganta vibra, como num zumbido. Depois feche a boca para o er. Sinta a língua tocando os dentes.
pages.tip: Treine “the, this, that, bother” em sequência, com a mão na garganta sentindo a vibração.
